title: Classification of fallers in Parkinson’s disease through machine learning based feature analysis
task: Machine learning classification of fall risk in Parkinson's disease patients
key_results: Extra Trees classifier with statistics-based feature selection achieves 88% internal and 89% external validation accuracy; three key domains identified: fear of falling, balance/gait, and autonomic dysfunction
comments: External validation from a second center strengthens credibility, though the modest sample size (98 external) and potential clinical heterogeneity warrant larger prospective studies.

outputs: faller vs. non-faller vs. control classification

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-domain integration (clinical + gait + autonomic) improves faller classification
hypotheses.result: Statistics-based feature selection identified three consistent domains with high accuracy
External validation accuracy (89%) similar to internal (88%)

title: Advancing target discovery through disease-specific integration of multi-modal target identification models and comprehensive benchmarking system
task: Disease-specific drug target identification and benchmarking
key_results: TargetPro predicts clinical-stage targets across 38 diseases with strong performance; TargetBench 1.0 evaluates target discovery models including LLMs on recovery of established targets
comments: The integration of multi-modal data with systematic benchmarking is valuable, though translational validation of novel candidates beyond established targets remains to be demonstrated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Disease-specific target identification models outperform generic approaches
hypotheses.result: TargetPro revealed disease-specific patterns supporting need for tailored detection

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-modal integration improves target prediction accuracy
hypotheses.result: Strong predictive performance on clinical-stage targets demonstrated

title: TMPA-HC: a two-stage heterogeneous multi-population algorithm with cooperative search for high-dimensional feature selection
task: High-dimensional feature selection via heterogeneous multi-population optimization
key_results: TMPA-HC achieves competitive feature selection performance with consistent convergence on benchmark datasets; reduces redundancy and computational cost versus standard swarm intelligence methods
comments: The two-stage framework with cooperative mechanisms is technically sound, but real-world high-dimensional application domains (e.g., genomics, imaging) and comparison to deep learning feature reduction methods are not discussed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-population cooperative search reduces feature redundancy
hypotheses.result: Selected subsets contain lower redundancy than single-population methods

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive control and restart mechanisms improve convergence in high dimensions
hypotheses.result: Consistent convergence and robustness demonstrated on benchmark datasets

title: Effects of hydrodynamic nonlocality on electromagnetic wave propagation and topological properties of magnetoplasmas
task: Analyze topological properties of nonlocal magnetized plasmas and edge modes
key_results: Derived explicit dispersion equations for bulk and edge modes in nonlocal magnetoplasmas; computed Chern numbers for nonlocal dispersion bands; demonstrated impact of nonlocality on topological protection of edge modes in Voigt configuration
comments: The work bridges plasma physics and topological band theory through hydrodynamic modeling, providing analytical foundations for previously unexplored nonlocal regimes.

model_io.model: Hydrodynamic plasma model with nonlocal effects

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hydrodynamic nonlocality affects the number and topological protection of edge modes compared to local models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; nonlocality shown to alter edge mode count and protection properties in magnetized plasmas

title: Long-range structural and magnetic coherence in embedded mesospin metamaterials
task: Fabricate structurally and magnetically coherent magnetic metamaterials via ion implantation
key_results: Demonstrated long-range antiferromagnetic order spontaneously developed in embedded iron-ion mesospin arrays without external annealing; sharp magnetic Bragg peaks observed via resonant X-ray scattering
comments: Ion implantation circumvents lithographic disorder, but scalability to device-relevant dimensions and coupling strength to photons remain to be quantified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Controlled ion implantation produces morphologically uniform mesospin arrays
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; uniform structural coherence achieved without lithographic topography

hypotheses.hypothesis: Embedded mesospins spontaneously order antiferromagnetically without external stimulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; as-fabricated state exhibits extended antiferromagnetic order
